Summary

This bubbles up the unsupported transitionable_display subfeature as a partial implementation for the property in general.

Test results and supporting details

This is an exceptional compromise between legibility and granularity, to reflect common use cases for the property in general, especially in the absence of feature detection.

The note is written to encourage future editors of this data to update both data points. Unfortunately, there's no way to comment on the subfeature to reference the parent in the same way.

Related issues

Fixes #26155

items.content_html:
Fixes #30474

<dialog closedby="any"> has a touch event propagation bug in Chrome 134–153
and Firefox 141+: tapping the backdrop closes the dialog but does not cancel
the event, causing click listeners on elements behind the backdrop to fire.

Changes:

  • Chrome: converted to array — clean entry for 154+ (fixed via
    bug 425579196), plus a 134–153 entry with a note
  • Firefox: added notes to the 141+ entry linking to
    bug 2022750 (still unfixed as of Firefox 156)
  • chrome_android, edge, and firefox_android correctly mirror their
    desktop entries — no additional changes needed
items.title: fix(html): add notes for dialog closedby=any touch propagation bug

items.content_html:
Fixes #30831

Adds three missing Permission Policy directive entries to html.elements.iframe.allow:

  • local-network: Chrome 145, Firefox 153, experimental: false
  • loopback-network: Chrome 145, Firefox 153, experimental: false
  • local-network-access: Chrome 142, Firefox false, experimental: true (legacy alias, superseded by the two above)

Firefox support verified via Bugzilla bug 1978550 (RESOLVED FIXED); network.lna.blocking defaults to true from the Firefox 153 release tag.

Note: http.headers.Permissions-Policy entries for these directives correctly remain false — Firefox has not implemented HTTP header parsing for Permissions-Policy (bug 1531012 is still open).
items.title: html/elements/iframe: add local-network, local-network-access, and loopback-network allow directives

items.content_html:
Summary

Adds api.console.context_static for the non-standard console.context() method, so the new MDN page requested in mdn/content#46017 has compat data.

Test results and supporting details

  • Chrome 61: the method was added in V8 commit v8/v8@701d79d08ad4 (June 2017), which is in V8 6.1 (6.1.534.32 contains it, 6.0.286.52 does not). V8 6.1 shipped in Chrome 61. Confirmed present in Chrome 154.
  • Firefox: not supported, https://bugzil.la/1948870 is still open.
  • Safari: not supported, https://webkit.org/b/293768 is still open.
  • Deno: typeof console.context is "undefined" in Deno 2.7.5 (tracking issue denoland/deno#29560).
  • Node.js 8.7.0: first release with V8 6.1 (deps/v8/include/v8-version.h), and its lib/internal/bootstrap_node.js already copies V8-only console methods onto the Node.js console. Marked as partial because messages are only sent to an attached inspector (nodejs/node#56634). I confirmed that behavior in Node.js 22.14 using inspector.Session and Runtime.consoleAPICalled.

npm run lint passes apart from the expected 404 warning for the mdn_url, which the mdn/content PR adds.

Related issues

Relates to mdn/content#46017
items.title: Add `console.context()` static method
